title: Sobolev mappings of Euclidean space and product structure
summary: We consider bounded open connected sets $Ω_1, Ω_2 \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and Sobolev maps $f: Ω_1 \times Ω_2 \subset \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n$, such that for almost every $x \in Ω_1 \times Ω_2$ the weak differential $\nabla f(x)$ is invertible and preserves or swaps the spaces $\mathbb{R}^n \times \{0\}$ and $\{0\} \times \mathbb{R}^n$. We show that if $n \ge 2$ and $f \in W^{1,2}$ then $f$ is split, i.e., $f(x_1, x_2) = (f_1(x_1), f_2(x_2))$ or $f(x_1, x_2) = (f_2(x_2), f_1(x_1))$.
